evals.prompt: Add Clerk to this current Next.js App Router repository. Keep the marketing home page public, require sign-in for /app, and protect the server data call too.
evals.expected_output: A framework-native Clerk integration based on the installed @clerk/nextjs version, with public and protected routing plus server-side authorization and runtime verification.
assertions: The agent inspects the framework, router mode, package manager, and installed Clerk version before selecting imports or middleware
The public page remains public while /app is protected
The protected data operation derives verified server-side Clerk state rather than trusting client identity
Secret credentials remain in server-only environment storage
Verification covers signed-out and signed-in server requests

evals.prompt: Our React Router SSR app has ClerkProvider in the browser, but loaders still return private data to signed-out requests. Repair the integration.
evals.expected_output: A React Router-specific server integration that preserves client rendering while enforcing identity and authorization in loaders.
assertions: The solution uses current first-party React Router Clerk guidance rather than generic React-only guidance
The agent checks the installed package version before choosing helpers
The loader or server boundary verifies Clerk state before reading private data
Client component visibility is not presented as authorization
The verification plan exercises a signed-out request directly against the loader

evals.prompt: Implement an API endpoint that only organization members with the records:manage permission can call. The request body includes orgId today.
evals.expected_output: A server-side organization authorization flow that derives trusted membership and permission state from Clerk and treats the submitted organization identifier only as a resource selector.
assertions: The client-provided orgId is not treated as proof of membership
The endpoint derives verified user and organization context at the server boundary
The required permission is enforced where the operation executes
Unauthenticated and forbidden states are distinct
The agent checks current Clerk organization authorization APIs against the installed SDK

evals.prompt: Create a Clerk webhook endpoint that mirrors user and organization changes into our database. Deliveries can be duplicated, delayed, or arrive out of order.
evals.expected_output: A verified raw-body webhook handler with explicit data ownership, idempotency, ordering protection, transactional updates, and recovery behavior.
assertions: The webhook signature is verified against the raw request body before trusting payload fields
The webhook secret stays server-side
Duplicate event delivery is idempotent
Older events cannot overwrite newer synchronized state
The design states which Clerk facts are mirrored and how missed events are recovered

evals.prompt: Gate an organization-owned export feature with Clerk Billing. Users should see the right UI, but direct API calls must also be blocked after cancellation or trial expiry.
evals.expected_output: An organization subscription and entitlement design with a server-owned gate, truthful UI projection, lifecycle handling, and provider-failure behavior.
assertions: The agent determines that the subscription owner is the organization
The API enforces the entitlement independently of UI visibility
Cancellation and trial expiry are covered
Webhook delay or temporary Clerk failure has an explicit behavior
Current Billing APIs are verified against canonical documentation and the installed package

evals.prompt: Set up Clerk end-to-end tests in CI for sign-up, sign-in, and one protected request. CI must not use production credentials or disable bot protection globally.
evals.expected_output: A provider-supported Clerk testing setup using isolated development credentials and testing facilities, with browser and server assertions.
assertions: Development or test Clerk credentials are separated from production
The solution uses Clerk-supported testing tokens or helpers where appropriate
Bot protection is not weakened globally for production
The tests cover sign-up or sign-in plus a protected server request
Provider dashboard configuration needed by CI is included in completion checks

evals.prompt: Upgrade this older Clerk integration. Do not assume the latest docs match our package. Replace deprecated middleware and imports safely.
evals.expected_output: A version-aware migration that inventories current packages and integration files, consults matching migration guidance, changes only supported symbols, and validates runtime behavior.
assertions: The agent records exact installed Clerk versions before editing
The agent checks matching released source or migration guidance for replacement symbols
Moving default-branch code is not treated as proof of released behavior
The existing integration is preserved except where migration requires change
Validation covers both browser flow and protected server behavior

evals.prompt: Use Clerk in a Go HTTP API. Verify the caller's session and ensure they belong to the organization that owns the requested record.
evals.expected_output: A version-aware official Go SDK integration with session verification, organization and resource authorization, secret handling, and direct handler tests.
assertions: The solution selects the official Clerk Go SDK and checks its installed major version
The session is verified server-side
Organization membership and resource ownership are both enforced
The request's organization identifier is not sufficient authorization
Tests cover unauthenticated, forbidden, and authorized requests
